result.title: Does Context Compression Preserve Refusal Alignment?
result.summary: Context compression reduces inference cost by encoding inputs into compact representations while preserving semantic content. An open question is whether semantic preservation alone is sufficient to maintain downstream behaviours such as refusal alignment. We investigate this question and find that encoder-based compression systematically weakens refusal behaviour in instruction-tuned language models, despite high reconstruction fidelity. This effect persists across model families and compression architectures. Mechanistic analysis shows that compression attenuates activation along the decoder's learned refusal direction. We further explore Memory Steering, a lightweight inference-time intervention that restores refusal rates to near-baseline levels without retraining and operates entirely in compressed representation space. These results demonstrate that semantic preservation does not guarantee behavioural preservation under compression, highlighting the need to explicitly preserve alignment-relevant features in compression-aware systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察基于编码器的上下文压缩在重构保真度较高时是否仍保持指令微调模型的拒答对齐，发现压缩会系统性削弱拒答行为，并归因于解码器拒答方向上的激活衰减，进而提出在压缩表示空间做推理时 Memory Steering 以恢复拒答率。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属纯文本压缩，但其「语义保真不等于行为保真」以及压缩表示空间的方向诊断与推理时干预，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 是否保留并实际驱动任务必要信息。
